newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia magazine faces government-backed closure.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia magazine faces government-backed closure.

text.p: The editor of an Indonesian magazine employing members of an unrecognised journalist group has had his licence to edit withdrawn, the government-backed journalists association said on Wednesday.

The move threatens Detektip & Romantika (D&R) magazine with closure. Under Indonesia's strict press laws a newspaper or publication cannot be printed unless its editor is approved by the official Indonesian Journalists Association (PWI).

Tarman Azzam, head of the PWI's Jakarta branch, said on Wednesday that his branch had cancelled the letter of recommendation of D&R editor Goesti Emran for employing members of the Alliance of Independent Journalists (AJI).

"The decision to cancel the recommendation among other reasons is because the D&R editor-in-chief has employed a number of journalists and editorial staff members who are not members of the PWI," Azzam said in a statement sent to Reuters. Azzam is editor of the afternoon daily Harian Terbit, part of the Pos Kota group of newspapers owned by Information Minister Harmoko, who has responsibility for approving publishing licences.
"If you lose such a recommendation, you are finished," an AJI member said, commenting on the PWI decision.
Neither Emran nor members of his staff were immediately available for comment.

"Before the cancellation of the recommendation for Goesti Emran was taken, officers of the PWI's Jakarta branch gave a number of verbal warnings and two strong written warnings. However these were not responded to as hoped by the PWI," Azzam said.
The weekly D&R, which has published a number of hard-hitting political stories and interviews in its 10 issues, employs a number of journalists formerly with the banned Tempo magazine.
In June 1994, the government banned Tempo and two other weeklies, DeTik and Editor, for being too outspoken.
An attempt to relaunch DeTik as Simponi in October 1994 failed after only one issue was published when the PWI withdrew its recommendation of the tabloid's editor-in-chief.
